answer: Make each key prove it holds its own working memory. At a beacon-picked minute each epoch, the node asks every key for 50 random entries from a 4 GB table derived from its key and the epoch seed, due within 1 second. Disk is too slow, so the table must sit in RAM. A 64 GB server can harbor about 15 keys, so a 1,000-key farm needs roughly 67 servers of real ferrous hardware, not one laptop. Two missed drills in ten epochs pause payouts. Results post each close, so no lotus of fake keys grows from one box.
